review_candidates.title: Robot Systems Integration Engineer
review_candidates.description: 该职位来源于猎聘 About the Role You own two things: the robot, and the devices we collect data with. The robot is a commercial humanoid that interacts with people in real venues. It arrives as hardware and an SDK; you make it a platform the rest of the team can build on: gesture, gaze and posture under software control, clean sensor streams out, a safety envelope for standing next to strangers, and a robot that is ready every morning of a demo. The devices are the capture kit we use to record people and robots for training data: fisheye cameras, wrist-worn IMU and hand-pose sensors, lightweight RGB-D, and the robot’s own sensors. You integrate them, keep them time-synced and calibrated, and keep them running at collection sites. You are the lowest layer of a small engineering team. An application engineer builds speech, dialogue and the operator console on the interfaces you expose; a hardware engineer designs the capture rigs you integrate. You work daily with the platform maker’s developers, and you are the person who knows what the robot can and cannot do. Key Responsibilities Integrate the robot Build and maintain the robot control layer using the platform’s SDK (DDS-based) and ROS 2 on NVIDIA Jetson: gesture, head and torso orientation for gaze, posture, locomotion-in-place, and safe transitions between them, timed to speech. Expose the robot to the application layer as a small, stable API: behavior primitives (greet, turn toward, point, beckon, hold a conversational posture, hand off) and a sensor event stream (speaker direction, person detected, approach distance, face and gaze). Get raw microphone and camera streams off the robot at the latency the speech and perception pipeline needs; work with the maker’s developers on access the SDK does not yet give. Own firmware and SDK updates, calibration, battery and thermal management, emergency stop and recovery, and the safety envelope for a humanoid among the public: speed and force limits, keep-out distances, what the robot does when touched. Integrate the capture devices Integrate capture sensors with their device SDKs and firmware, with hardware time sync across modalities, and execute the calibration protocol set by the hardware engineer. Record demonstration and teleoperation data from the robot itself (joint states, cameras, audio) in the format the data pipeline expects. Deploy and keep it running Write the test plan for each venue, run it on site, and triage what fails: document, reproduce, fix or hand off across hardware and software. Instrument the robot and devices with health telemetry and a daily readiness check a colleague can run without you; send a weekly site-health summary to engineering. Package the platform layer so a second robot, in another location, comes up from a known configuration in a day, and write the runbook that goes with it. Skills & Experience Required 3+ years building software that ran on real robots in the real world, not simulation alone. Hands-on experience with a commercial humanoid or legged platform: deploying, debugging and controlling it through the maker’s SDK, ROS 2 and NVIDIA Jetson, including joint and posture commands and trajectory timing. Strong C++ and Python; comfortable with DDS or similar middleware, Linux, real-time constraints and embedded compute. Experience getting sensor data (cameras, microphones, IMU) off a robot or device and into a software pipeline, with hardware time synchronization. Comfortable debugging hardware under deadline and running a robot safely around members of the public. Native-level Mandarin and professional working English; eligible to work in China. Preferred Multi-sensor calibration (camera intrinsics and extrinsics, IMU, depth) and wearable or egocentric capture hardware. Teleoperation or motion-capture rigs, and recording demonstration data for robot learning (LeRobot, RLDS or similar conventions). Humanoid foundation-model stacks (e.g. NVIDIA Isaac GR00T or a robot maker’s open models) or a robot maker’s developer ecosystem. Gesture retargeting from motion capture or animation, or working with animators. Functional safety or risk assessment for collaborative or mobile robots. Robots that interact with the public: retail, museums, hospitality, healthcare, education. SLAM, localization and navigation on a mobile or legged robot, or real-to-sim capture and reconstruction (LiDAR scanning, photogrammetry, Gaussian splatting). Autonomous navigation and venue simulation come later in the program, and the platform layer you own is where they land. What success looks like First month: robot up in a real venue with the SDK integrated; greet, turn-toward and point primitives callable from the application layer; raw audio and camera streams at usable latency. First 3 months: a live, multilingual interaction demo on the real robot in front of an audience. Not polished: the robot greets, turns toward, points and hands off with gesture and gaze timed to speech in two languages, with an operator in the loop; zero safety incidents; robot available on every scheduled demo day. By 6 months: capture devices integrated with cross-modality sync drift inside the agreed tolerance; a second robot brought up in another location from your packaged configuration in one day; readiness check and runbook in use without you present.

review_candidates.title: Hotel Manager
review_candidates.description: Department: Hotel Management Location: Tanzania - Manyara Description About Kempinski At Kempinski, we don't just offer stays; we curate moments. As a hospitality organization, anchored in a legacy of elegance and a pioneering spirit, we have grown into a collection of iconic hotels and resorts around the world, each a landmark in its own right. From grand palaces steeped in history to contemporary masterpieces of design, Kempinski is where impeccable service meets authentic local experiences. We empower our people to be artisans of hospitality, fostering an environment where passion is nurtured, individuality is celebrated, and every detail is thoughtfully considered. Joining Kempinski means becoming part of a family that is dedicated to creating memories that last a lifetime for our guests, and a fulfilling and enriching career for our team. If you are driven by excellence, inspired by the art of hospitality, and seek to contribute to a legacy of luxury, we invite you to explore the exceptional opportunities that await you at Kempinski Hotels. We invite you to be part of our story. How You Will Make a Difference; What We’re Looking For The Hotel Manager serves as the on-site general executive for Kempinski Msasa Lodge, Lake Manyara . Leading an intimate 25-key boutique safari lodge, this role is responsible for translating Kempinski’s signature European luxury service into an authentic, remote wilderness setting. The position demands an agile, hands-on leader who functions as the primary host for travellers while maintaining end-to-end oversight of lodge operations, financial performance, supply chain logistics, remote engineering/utilities infrastructure, team development, and conservation partnership compliance. Key Responsibilities 1. Executive Operations & Remote Camp Logistics Direct all day-to-day operations across Rooms/Tented Suites, Food & Beverage, Guiding/Safari Activities, Engineering, Security, and Spa/Wellness. Manage remote logistics, including cold-chain transport, off-grid inventory minimums, fuel management, and bush supply lines to ensure uninterrupted 5-star operations. Oversee physical plant management: solar PV arrays, generator backup systems, borehole water filtration, wastewater treatment, and tent structural preservation. 2. Luxury Guest Experience Lead bespoke check-in experiences, personalised game-drive planning, and hosted bush dinners. Uphold Kempinski service standards and Leading Quality Assurance (LQA) benchmarks tailored to boutique safari camp operations. Oversee unique safari guest touch-points: fly-camping setups, open-vehicle game drives, sun downers, bush breakfasts, and naturalist-led walking safaris. Resolve guest concerns proactively and monitor guest satisfaction metrics (GSS, TripAdvisor, luxury travel network feedback). 3. Supply Chain & Logistics Design and supervise an integrated procurement and supply chain pipeline linking sourcing hubs to remote airstrips and overland delivery corridors. Manage central inventory models to mitigate stock shortages caused by seasonal rains, rough road infrastructure, and park access restrictions. Audit and oversee aviation transfer logistics, guest meet-and-greet services at bush airstrips, and luggage transit flows across properties. 4. Commercial Strategy & Financial Performance Formulate and manage the annual operating budget (OPEX) and capital expenditure plans (CAPEX) with finance leadership. Drive Gross Operating Profit (GOP) through rigorous cost-control across food waste, logistics, energy consumption, and labor efficiency without compromising luxury. Partner with Central Sales & Marketing to optimise boutique lodge distribution, maintaining strong relationships with destination management companies (DMCs), safari operators, and luxury travel consortia. 5. Government, Authority & Community Relations Act as the primary executive liaison with Tanzania National Parks (TANAPA), the Ministry of Natural Resources and Tourism, and local District Councils. Ensure 100% statutory compliance regarding concession lease agreements, environmental impact audits (NEMC), and annual park operating permits. Build positive relationships with local pastoralist and agricultural communities, driving community outreach, local purchasing programs, and dispute resolution. 6. People & Culture Leadership Drive regional talent acquisition and and developing local management talent. Foster a positive workplace culture across remote staff villages, overseeing employee accommodations, recreation, canteen services, wellness, and rotational leave rosters. Supervise the Kempinski training curriculum, instilling European luxury hospitality service standards tailored to East African warmth and storytelling. Job Requirements Bachelor’s degree in Hospitality Management, Business Administration, or related discipline. Master’s degree is a plus. Minimum 6–8 years of luxury hospitality leadership, with at least 3–4 years as Hotel Manager, Camp Manager, or Assistant GM in an ultra-luxury safari lodge or remote boutique resort. Demonstrated pre-opening or re branding experience in remote African destinations is required. Demonstrated track record working within national park and wildlife conservancy regulatory frameworks. Proven success running high-end tented camps, off-grid utilities, and bush logistical operations. Culturally sensitive mentor dedicated to uplifting local communities. About Kempinski Kempinski emphasises talent development and offers career progression within its global network, with properties in over 30 countries. There are opportunities to work in diverse cultural environments whilst continuing your professional growth. We are proud to foster a culture where employees feel valued, heard, and are empowered to deliver exceptional guest experiences. Be part of a legacy, build your future. Discover the possibilities at Kempinski. Equal Opportunities As an equal opportunity employer, Kempinski embraces diversity and is committed to creating a workplace where everyone feels valued and has the opportunity to succeed. Kempinski is committed to equal employment opportunities regardless of race, colour, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability or veteran status.
